breakfast.name: Belgian Waffles (Liege-Style Waffles)
breakfast.description: Belgian waffles that are thicker and have deeper indentations than standard waffles, with crispy exterior and soft interior. Served with chocolate, fruit, or whipped cream
ingredients: Pearl sugar (or coarse sugar for topping)
instructions: Sift together flour, baking powder, and cornstarch
Beat egg whites in large bowl until stiff peaks form
Transfer to another bowl
Beat egg yolks with sugar until pale and thick (about 3 minutes)
Gently fold in flour mixture alternating with milk
Stir in melted butter and vanilla extract
Carefully fold in beaten egg whites in 2 batches
Preheat Belgian waffle maker and lightly oil
Pour batter into waffle maker
Sprinkle pearl sugar on top before closing
Cook according to machine instructions (typically 3-4 minutes) until golden and crispy
Serve immediately while warm
Top with chocolate, fruit, whipped cream, or eaten plain
breakfast.notes: Cornstarch is secret ingredient making waffles extra crispy. Authentic Belgian waffles made from dough (not batter) with pearl sugar hidden inside
breakfast.fun_fact: Belgian waffles are thicker and have deeper indentations than standard waffles. Cornstarch creates extra crispy texture found in authentic Belgian waffles
alternatives: Make with chocolate chips in batter
Make with buckwheat flour for nuttier flavor

items.name: Pearl sugar (or coarse sugar)
items.note: For topping — the signature caramelized crunch

stepHelp: Sifting keeps the batter light and lump-free — cornstarch especially clumps if you skip it.
Stiff peaks means the whites hold their shape when you lift the beater out — this is what makes the waffles light instead of dense.
About 3 minutes on medium-high — the mixture should fall in a ribbon and hold its shape briefly when you lift the beater.
Fold, don't stir — a rubber spatula, cutting through the center and turning the bowl, keeps the batter from deflating.
Fold in a third of the whites first to loosen the batter, then fold in the rest gently — this keeps the air you worked for.
The pearl sugar caramelizes against the hot iron — that's where the crackly sweet crust comes from.
Resist opening the iron early — steam needs to escape and the crust needs to set, usually signaled by the steam slowing down.

variations.title: Chocolate Chip
variations.text: Fold mini chocolate chips into the batter right before the egg whites for pockets of melted chocolate.

variations.title: Buckwheat Twist
variations.text: Swap a third of the flour for buckwheat flour for a nuttier, more rustic flavor.

variations.title: Savory Route
variations.text: Skip the sugar and vanilla, add a pinch of extra salt, and top with a fried egg and bacon for a savory waffle.

variations.title: Overnight Batter
variations.text: Mix everything but the egg whites the night before and refrigerate — whip and fold in fresh whites the next morning.

variations.title: Stuffed Waffle
variations.text: Press a square of chocolate or a dollop of Nutella into the center of the batter before closing the iron.

serveWith.intro: Belgian waffles are rich enough to anchor a whole brunch spread on their own, but a few classic sides make it a proper occasion.

items.title: Whipped Cream & Berries
items.text: Classic for a reason — the tartness of fresh berries cuts through the rich, sweet waffle.

items.title: Melted Chocolate
items.text: A traditional Belgian topping — drizzle warm chocolate right over the pearl sugar crust.

items.title: Vanilla Ice Cream
items.text: Turns breakfast into dessert; the warm waffle melts the ice cream into a sauce.

items.title: Strong Coffee
items.text: A dark roast coffee balances the waffle's sweetness.

items.title: Fresh Fruit Compote
items.text: Warm stewed fruit soaks into the waffle's pockets beautifully.

expertTips.title: Keep Butter Warm, Not Hot
expertTips.text: Melted butter that's still warm folds into the batter more evenly than butter that's cooled and started to firm up.

expertTips.title: Don't Overmix
expertTips.text: Stop folding as soon as you don't see streaks of egg white — overmixing knocks the air back out.

expertTips.title: Preheat Fully
expertTips.text: A fully hot iron is what gives you the crisp exterior; a lukewarm iron steams the waffle instead of searing it.

expertTips.title: Real Pearl Sugar
expertTips.text: Regular granulated sugar will melt away — pearl sugar (Belgian sugar pearls) is formulated to survive the heat and stay crunchy.

storage.title: Fridge
storage.text: Cooked waffles keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

storage.title: Freezer
storage.text: Freeze cooled waffles in a single layer, then transfer to a zip-top bag for up to 2 months.

storage.title: Reheating
storage.text: Reheat from frozen in a toaster or 350°F oven until warmed through and the crust re-crisps — microwaving will make them soft.

breakfast.makeAhead: Make a full batch on the weekend, cool completely, and freeze in a single layer before bagging. Toast straight from frozen on a busy morning for a fresh-tasting waffle in minutes.

faqs.q: Can I make the batter ahead of time?
faqs.a: Mix the dry and wet components separately and refrigerate overnight, but whip and fold in the egg whites fresh right before cooking for the best rise.

faqs.q: What if I don't have pearl sugar?
faqs.a: Coarse or turbinado sugar is the closest substitute — it won't fully caramelize the same way but adds crunch and sweetness.

faqs.q: Why are my waffles dense instead of light?
faqs.a: Likely the egg whites were overmixed into the batter, or not beaten to stiff peaks in the first place — both knock the air out that makes these waffles light.

faqs.q: Can I use a regular waffle iron?
faqs.a: Yes, though the waffles will be thinner and cook faster — check for golden color starting around 2-3 minutes instead of 3-4.

dinner.name: Stoemp (Belgian Mashed Vegetables with Sausage)
dinner.description: Belgian comfort food - mashed potatoes with vegetables and sausage
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water 15 minutes
Add carrots and leeks; continue cooking 10 minutes
Add onions; cook final 5 minutes until all vegetables tender
Meanwhile, pan-fry sausages in separate skillet 12-15 minutes until cooked through; keep warm
Drain vegetables, reserving 100ml cooking liquid
Return vegetables to pot, add butter and minced garlic
Mash until desired consistency (some prefer chunky, some prefer smooth)
Gradually add warm milk and reserved cooking liquid to reach creamy texture
Season with salt, white pepper, and nutmeg
Fold in parsley
Serve in bowls with sausage on top
Drizzle with pan drippings from sausages if desired
dinner.notes: Traditionally served as working person's meal. Cooking vegetables together creates flavor unity
dinner.fun_fact: Stoemp is considered authentic Belgian peasant food, simple but deeply satisfying comfort food
